summary: Latency regressions and request timeouts for repeated prompts — KV/prefix cache misses causing slower-than-expected repeat prompts
description:
Issue summary: Multiple API requests for the same conversation context are observing higher-than-expected token latency and intermittent request timeouts on repeated prompts. Impact: Customer reports increased tail latency (~500-800ms additional per request) and occasional 504s for conversational flows that historically benefited from prefix/KV cache reuse. Environment: Production, us-east-1, dedicated capacity (NovaForms dedicated pool). Initial detection: Customer reported on 2026-03-02 after rolling a high-throughput conversation workload.

Observed behaviour: First request in a conversation appears normal; subsequent repeated prompts that should hit warmed KV/prefix cache frequently miss or trigger partial rebuilds of KV state, leading to higher CPU/GPU kernel invocation and increased latency. Some requests hit timeouts at the edge (504) when combined with client-side low timeouts.

Impact scope: NovaForms affected across all routes using redwood-v2-large; preliminary ATL shows 8% of requests for this customer exceeded previous P95 by >400ms. No broad platform-wide incident reported yet but similar signals found for a small set of other dedicated customers in us-east-1.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use a conversation with pinned model redwood-v2-large and typical prompt size (approx 1k tokens).
2) Send an initial seed prompt (expect normal latency ~200ms per token).
3) Send repeated short follow-up prompts that should reuse prefix/KV cache (expect sub-100ms incremental).
4) Observe higher latency (400-800ms) and occasional 504/timeouts on follow-ups; correlate with serving-runtime and cache miss logs.
logs: 2026-03-02T14:12:03Z [serving-runtime] request_id=abc123 route=converse model=redwood-v2-large kv_cache_hit=false cold_kv_build=true kernel_exec_ms=580
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: recent change to cache eviction heuristic in runtime release v1.74 increased prefix cache churn under certain sequence-length distributions.
Checked recent deploys: runtime v1.74 rolled to dedicated pools in us-east-1 on 2026-03-01 (linked PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1250).
Observed correlation between deploy time and customer-reported spike. Metrics show increased KV miss rate for long-context conversations where average sequence length > 800 tokens.

SRE reproduction: ran synthetic workload against a dedicated pool and reproduced elevated kernel_exec_ms and kv_cache_hit=false traces when concurrent conversation count > 60 and sequence length variance high.

Hypothesis refined: eviction policy change reduces retention of prefix KV entries when memory pressure is perceived; combined with a change in kernel scheduling, this causes extra work to rebuild KV state rather than reuse it.
Mitigation options considered: (a) rollback v1.74 to v1.73 for affected pools, (b) tune eviction threshold for dedicated pools, (c) implement a forced warm-path for pinned model routes.
workaround: Applied temporary mitigation on 2026-03-03: increased KV cache retention threshold for NovaForms dedicated pool and enabled forced warm-on-first-request for affected routes. Initial telemetry shows p95 latency returned closer to baseline for this customer.
resolution: Mitigation applied and performance restored for NovaForms. Root cause traced to eviction heuristic in runtime v1.74 causing premature eviction of prefix KV entries under specific sequence-length and concurrency patterns. Follow-up actions: revert eviction heuristic in next patch release, add targeted unit/integration tests for KV retention, and add an observability alert for sudden KV miss-rate increases. Linked INT-4234 for orchestrating rollback in other affected pools.
